title: Offer the strongest evidence
statement: When students pick evidence from a set, the strongest evidence must be in the set, and the rubric must not credit evidence they can't pick.
example: In two lessons, three tap-the-evidence items left out the strongest sentence or credited one students couldn't tap.
detail: Reviews of tap-the-evidence items in two Grade 3 lessons found three faults (`shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U2-L1-review.md`, `shadow/content-eval/reports/G3-U1-L14-review.md`). The sentence linking a plant's job to its survival was missing from the tappable list, a rubric accepted a sentence that isn't one of the tappable spans, and the strongest clue in a paragraph couldn't be tapped. All three were judgment calls in the reviews.

evidence.quote: - The sentence that links the job to survival, *"This natural way of spreading helps plants survive in new places."*, isn't in the tappable list at all.
The rubric accepts *"He stayed close, guarded Mole's back"*, but that sentence isn't one of the tappable evidence spans.
- **p20 tap-the-clue:** *"I am the reason you have all been dragged into this mess."* is the strongest "owning it" clue in the paragraph, but it isn't tappable as a clue.
